from rich.highlighter import ReprHighlighter
from rich.text import Text

highlighter = ReprHighlighter()
test_urls = [
    "https://example.com/~user",
    "https://example.com/~user/page",
    "http://example.com/~test",
    "file:///home/user/~test",
]

for url in test_urls:
    text = Text(url)
    highlighter.highlight(text)
    # The text object now contains spans. 
    # We want to check if the URL was highlighted.
    # For ReprHighlighter, it should use a style starting with 'repr.'
    # The url regex in ReprHighlighter is part of a combined regex.
    # Let's see what spans are created.
    print(f"URL: {url} -> Spans: {text.spans}")

# To verify that it actually matched the whole thing, we can check the span bounds.
for url in test_urls:
    text = Text(url)
    highlighter.highlight(text)
    if text.spans:
        span = text.spans[0]
        print(f"URL: {url} -> Matched: {url[span.start:span.end]}")
    else:
        print(f"URL: {url} -> No match")

I've updated `rich/highlighter.py` to allow tildes in URLs and verified the fix with a reproduction script.

The tilde character (`~`) was missing from the URL regular expression in `rich/highlighter.py`, causing URLs containing tildes to be incorrectly highlighted. I added `~` to the character class of the URL regex in the `ReprHighlighter` class.

```python
# Before
r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#]*)"

# After
r"(?P<url>(file|https|http|ws|wss)://[-0-9a-zA-Z$_+!`(),.?/;:&=%#~]*)"
```

Verified the fix using a reproduction script that checks if `ReprHighlighter` correctly identifies URLs with tildes.
